html:
The Battle of Maiwand was fought on 27 July 1880 west of Kandahar, in southern Afghanistan, where an Afghan army under Ayub Khan defeated a British and Indian brigade in the Second Anglo-Afghan War.

Britain had invaded again in 1878 to stop Russian influence, as in the first war. At Maiwand Ayub Khan's larger force, with artillery and tribal fighters, broke the brigade, which lost about a thousand men and fled to Kandahar.

Afghans remember Malalai of Maiwand, a young woman said to have rallied the fighters with a song and her veil as a banner before she was killed. Many schools and hospitals are named after her. The British relieved Kandahar soon after, but left Afghanistan the next year, keeping control of its foreign affairs, and later drew the Durand Line. Arthur Conan Doyle made Dr Watson a veteran wounded at Maiwand, in the first Sherlock Holmes story.
